> Rule: 1.1.2 - Verify that the application performs output encoding and escaping either as a final step before being used by the interpreter for which it is intended or by the interpreter itself.

SPAs have complex data flows ( from state management to components to APIs), and ensuring that encoding happens as the “**final step**” can be challenging.

comments.body: Challenging or not, this is a key architecture concept for output encoding and escaping. I am not sure there is much to be done here.

My concern is not about the security principle itself. It is mainly about verification clarity when framework-based rendering is involved.

1. How should this requirement be interpreted or verified in SPA frameworks?
2. How should this requirement be interpreted on the server side application vs spa frameworks?

labels.name: Will be closed if no response/opposite arguments

title: Clarification 1.1.2: How  requirement apply to Single Page Applications (SPA) architectures
